subject: Post-call: end-to-end latency alignment + next steps (p95/p99)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Green <samantha@veridian.ai>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: end-to-end latency alignment + next steps (p95/p99)

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared expectations on p95/p99 qualification for hosted vs your incumbent provider:

Summary of outcome:
- Veridian is prioritizing user-facing inference latency (search/assist flows) with current acceptance targets of p95 < 220ms and p99 < 520ms measured end-to-end (~client to client).
- You want an apples-to-apples hosted-hosted vs incumbent comparison across both streaming and non-streaming endpoints, and across typical payload distributions.

Proposed scope for the qualification run:
1) Metrics and measurement: measure end-to-end latency at the client SDK boundary. Provide both p95 and p99, plus distribution plots and sample traces for tail events. Include both cold and warm-key scenarios (cold = empty KV-cache; warm = steady-state).
2) Traffic profile: run three traffic mixes — 70% short prompts (~40 tokens), 25% mid (~120 tokens), 5% long with streaming (>512 tokens). Attachments include sample_payloads_1000.jsonl.
3) Concurrency/throughput envelope: test 1, 5, 20, 50 concurrent connections (per regional egress) and step up sustained QPS until we hit either target latency SLO or system saturation.
4) Streaming behavior: for streaming endpoints, capture chunk emission latency and first-byte latency separately vs final-token latency.
5) Failure/fallback scenarios: include a capacity-fallback test where requests are rerouted to a lower-cost variant to observe graceful degradation.

Next steps / owners (proposed):
- Veridian: confirm sample payload set + representative client SDK(s) and provide any client-side batching logic you have (due: Thu 2027-03-11). (owner: Samantha)
- Redwood: deliver test plan and runbook + provisioning of hosted test endpoints and credentials (attachment: redwood_e2e_latency_testplan.pdf). We'll also provide a small load agent you can run from your AWS account if you prefer client-side generation. (owner: Irene)
- Joint: 2-day test window (we propose Mon/Tue, 2027-03-15/16) and a follow-up review on Wed 2027-03-17.

Questions we raised in the call (we need clarity):
- Do you measure p95/p99 at the same boundary we propose (client SDK socket -> SDK receive complete)? If not, please share your measurement point so we can align.
- Are there authentication/egress IP allowlist constraints for us to run agents from your VPC?

Attachments: redwood_e2e_latency_testplan.pdf (3 pages - test matrix, measurement scripts), sample_payloads_1000.jsonl (JSONL, 1k payloads representative of your traffic mix)

Thanks — I’ll stand up the test endpoints once we have the payloads and your signoff on the window.

—
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samantha Green <samantha@veridian.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: end-to-end latency alignment + next steps (p95/p99)

Thanks, Irene — this is exactly what we discussed. A couple clarifications:
- We currently measure at our edge proxy (TLS terminate) so our numbers include a tiny bit of TLS + network hops before model platform. We'll export a mapping of where we capture p95/p99 today.
- For streaming, our clients render partials as they arrive; first-byte latency is our primary KPI for user experience.

I'll upload the payload set + a whitebox client SDK snippet to the Drive link you shared by end-of-day tomorrow. For the test window, Mon/Tue works; prefer morning start so we can validate provisioning the first day.

—
Samantha Green
Head of Product, Veridian.ai
Samantha.Green@veridian.ai

Appreciate the quick confirmation, Samantha. A few additions after syncing with Ben and Marissa this morning:

Action items we’ll include in the test plan before provisioning:
- Measurement alignment doc: we’ll add a short section mapping measurement boundaries (client SDK vs edge vs proxy) and provide guidance so you can translate your existing numbers to the SDK boundary.
- Sampling/tracing: we’ll instrument distributed traces with a shared trace-id header so we can stitch client->edge->model traces and isolate where tail events originate.
- Warmup policy: include a 5-minute KV warmup phase before capturing steady-state metrics and a separate cold-run set.
- Quantiles and confidence: we’ll compute p95/p99 with 95% confidence intervals and include raw sample counts for transparency.

Logistics:
- Please drop the payloads and the preferred client SDKs to the Drive folder at the link above. If you prefer, run Redwood’s load agent inside your VPC and we’ll collect metrics remotely (we can provide AMI + quickstart).
- Ben will be the REDWOOD point for run-day incident coordination; Marissa will take notes and own the post-test report.

If everything looks good, we’ll finalize the test windows and share ephemeral credentials for the hosted endpoints by Friday EOD.

Best,
Irene
